text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>Ayotzinapa: 10 new suspects identified — and detained</u>

President Sheinbaum told the families of the 43 that new cell-phone and forensic analysis identified "10 people who had not been linked to the case" and made calls tied to the forced disappearance — all now in custody. She asked that the findings be published before the September 26 anniversary and pledged to press pending extraditions from abroad. Twelve years on, the 4T keeps pulling the thread earlier governments cut.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Morena hands the Senate gavel to a veteran — and stands up a Women's Secretariat</u>

Veteran senator Higinio Martínez takes the Senate presidency on September 1 by consensus of Morena's caucus, as Laura Itzel Castillo leaves the post to head the newly created federal Secretaría de las Mujeres under President Sheinbaum. A governing bloc reshuffling its own leadership and standing up a new ministry for women in the same move.

FOX: Drug Cartels Are "Foreign Terrorists" — Trump Approves Military Action August 26, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Fox cheers Trump's "foreign terrorist" label as the key that unlocks lethal US strikes on cartels — boats in the Pacific, drones over the Rio Grande. 🔍 The word doing the work: "terrorist." 💀 Left out: Sheinbaum has ruled out any US operation on Mexican soil — "there is not going to be an invasion" — and moved to write that veto into the constitution. • cartels are "foreign terrorist organizations" • Trump commits to "lethal" force against cartels Source

The detail it buries: the cartel's new leader, El Mencho's heir, is a US citizen born in Santa Ana who bought the place at 26 for $250K. 💀 The headline US media avoids: the CJNG's top boss is American, and his "refuge" is Orange County — not Michoacán. • bought "a ranch in Hemet, California... for just $250,000" • his "refuge to escape from Santa Ana, where he was born"

text: ‍WSJ: Sheinbaum Is Taking More Control as U.S. Pressures Mexico August 28, 2026 | 🔴 📰 WSJ: "each time Sheinbaum gives Trump an inch, he demands a mile." Its read on a president who prosecutes narco-politicians and trims tariffs to keep US troops off Mexican soil? A power grab. 🔍 She's dismantling criminal-political networks partly to preempt the US military action Trump keeps dangling — a defensive play the piece narrates only as ambition. • "each time Sheinbaum gives Trump an inch, he demands a mile" • "forcing Mexico's president into a corner"

🇲🇽💵 <u>The superpeso shrugs off the Fed</u>

Fed chair Kevin Warsh used his Jackson Hole speech to signal more rate hikes, pushing the dollar back above 17 pesos (17.03). Even so, El Financiero notes the peso is still up 5.29% this year — from 18.01 to 17.05 per dollar — outrunning its emerging-market peers. One hawkish speech doesn’t erase a year of the superpeso.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PAN keeps collapsing — now it’s lost Coahuila</u>

Mexico’s right-wing PAN just lost its official registration in Coahuila after scraping barely 2.1% in June’s local elections, erasing its seats in the state congress. Once the party of Fox and Calderón, it can no longer clear the threshold to legally exist in a northern state it used to contest.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Larrea still won’t pay to clean the river he poisoned</u>

Twelve years after Grupo México dumped copper sulfate into the Río Sonora — the worst toxic spill in the country’s mining history — Germán Larrea’s empire is refusing to hand over the final 500 million pesos it owes for water-treatment plants. Federal authorities set an August 21 deadline and are threatening to reactivate the criminal complaint against Mexico’s richest man.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Declassified: how the CIA sized up Salinas</u>

Newly declassified CIA files from 1986-88 profile Carlos Salinas de Gortari — who took power through the fraudulent 1988 election — as an “ambitious technocrat” with “good family connections” and a Harvard doctorate. Washington’s spies tracked Mexico’s succession closely, at first preferring Manuel Bartlett for his better US ties.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Fuel-theft network ran through Navy brass and the airport</u>

The FGR says the “huachicol fiscal” fuel-smuggling ring led by ex-Navy brothers Roberto and Fernando Farías Laguna reached the customs house of Mexico City’s international airport and six seaports. Nineteen former Marines are implicated — an admiral, two rear admirals, two vice admirals and 14 captains — accused of faking import papers to dodge fuel taxes.
